subject: Post-demo follow-up: Neurolytics data-retention carveout & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Liam Turner <l.turner@neurolytics.com>, Neurolytics Security <security@neurolytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T23:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: data-retention carveout & next steps

Hi Liam / Security team —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum:

Summary of asks you raised on the call:
- Neurolytics wants a short-term proof of concept with a scoped data-retention exception: 0-retention for PII fields, and a shortened KV / request log TTL for non-PII telemetry (proposal: 7 days)
- Data residency requirement: US-only hosting for inference and logs
- Audit evidence needs: SOC 2 summary, access/audit logs export, and a data-flow diagram showing where plaintext PII may be staged
- KMS-integrated encryption for key management and optional HSM for enterprise customers

What Im sending after this email:
1) Our SOC 2 one-pager (attached)
2) A short spreadsheet with three retention options and implied operational trade-offs (attached)
3) A pre-filled MSP questionnaire with the security fields you highlighted — please flag gaps

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Neurolytics security: confirm whether the 0-retention clause needs to be applied to tokenized identifiers or all raw text (Liam / security) — due by EOD Thursday
- Redwood: well scope a narrow POC config (US-only, 0-retention for PII, 7-day TTL for other logs) and share a configuration page + estimated cost delta (Aditya) — by Monday
- Legal/procurement: if Neurolytics wants a written carveout, our legal team can draft an MSA rider; well need a short list of the systems that will send data (Neurolytics)

Attachment stubs: neurolytics-msp-questionnaire.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, proposed-ttl-options.xlsx

Short ask: can you confirm by Thursday whether the 0-retention needs to cover hashed identifiers or strictly PII-free-ingestion? If hashed identifiers are considered PII, well need to adjust the POC and logging windows.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform

From: Liam Turner <l.turner@neurolytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Neurolytics Security <security@neurolytics.com>, Sanjay Patel <s.patel@neurolytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: data-retention carveout & next steps

Thanks Aditya — helpful recap. A few clarifications from security and product:

1) PII scope: We consider any direct identifiers (name, email, SSN) PII and want 0-retention. Hashed identifiers used for de-duplication are currently considered acceptable only if the hashing occurs client-side and we retain the salt. We need to understand whether Redwood receives raw input before hashing in the default integration.

2) Telemetry TTL: 7 days is a good starting point, but product wants the option to toggle 24/72/168 hours in the POC. Can you support a parameterized TTL per-application?

3) Logs & audit exports: we need a way to request a signed export of access logs for the POC window. Is that something you can provide on-demand?

I attached the MSP questionnaire (filled-in sections) and flagged a few items for your security team. Also attached a short one-pager describing constraints from our compliance group.

Our timeline: wed like the POC config by next Tuesday; legal will review any rider after POC results.

—Liam
Liam Turner, Head of Product Security, Neurolytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T15:28:00Z
Subject: RE: Post-demo follow-up: data-retention carveout & next steps

Copying Neha for technical scope. Action items Ill take on:
- Build a POC runbook that wires a dedicated US-only inference pool, configures per-field retention rules, and surfaces where hashing/client-side tokenization needs to occur.
- Add a parameterized TTL switch (24/72/168 hours) to the POC config; well document cost delta for each option in the sheet.
- Prepare an access-log export endpoint for signed on-demand pulls (format: ndjson) and note any limitations.

Neha: can you confirm whether our current runtime supports per-field zero-retention (i.e., drop fields before persisting KV cache) or if we need a custom filter in the ingestion layer? If the latter, include rough effort estimate.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam Turner <l.turner@neurolytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T13:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Post-demo follow-up: data-retention carveout & next steps

Marissa / Aditya — quick update from an engineering perspective: we can implement per-field zero-retention at the ingestion proxy (recommended) in the POC. Notes:

- Approach: add a lightweight JSON schema-based filter that strips configured PII fields before data reaches the runtime; this preserves ability to accept hashed tokens when client-side hashing is used.
- TTLs: runtime already supports TTL configuration per-keyspace; exposing 24/72/168 hour options is a small UI/ops lift for POC.
- Audit exports: we can enable signed ndjson exports for the POC; retention policy will govern how long those exports remain available (well keep signed exports for 30 days unless legal requests otherwise).
- Cost/delta: estimated engineering/configuration effort ~3 engineer-days; infra delta for US-only dedicated pool + 24hr TTL is roughly +18% on per-token cost in our estimate table (Marissa will attach numbers).

Neha Kapoor
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

P.S. Aditya — I drafted the POC config file and uploaded to the secure drive: https://drive.redwood.com/POCs/Neurolytics/po c-config-20260909.json (internal).
